. . .
NORWAY — Twenty three people died in Norway within days of receiving their first dose of the Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine, with 13 of those deaths being elderly nursing home patients, evidently relayed to the side effects of the shots, Norwegian health officials said.

Officials believe that the vaccine itself didn’t cause the actual deaths but common adverse reactions such as fever and nausea “may have contributed to a fatal outcome in some frail patients,” Norwegian Medicines Agency chief physician Sigurd Hortemo said Friday in a statement. 

All 13 nursing home patients were at least 80 years old and were expected to only have months to live.

Officials aren’t expressing any extreme worries due to the number of deaths were mostly elderly and frail nursing home patients, however they are adapting their administration on who now should receive the vaccine.

“We are not alarmed by this,” Steinar Madsen, an agency medical director told Norwegian broadcaster NRK. “It is quite clear that these vaccines have very little risk, with a small exception for the frailest patients.”

These deaths comes as more than 30,000 people in Norway have received the first shot of the Pfizer or Moderna coronavirus vaccine since December, according to official figures.

Reportedly, 29 people, 21 women and eight men had suffered side effects, including the 13 people who died. 

Excluding the deceased, nine suffered serious side effects such as allergic reactions, strong discomfort and severe fever — while the other seven had less serious ones. 

In total, there have been more than 57,000 COVID-19 cases with 500 coronavirus-related deaths reported in Norway, according to Johns Hopkins University.

“Una nueva revisión de un equipo dirigido por alergólogos de la Escuela de Medicina de Harvard con sede en el Hospital General de Massachusetts ofrece la tranquilidad de que las dos vacunas COVID-19 actualmente aprobadas (Pfizer-BioNTech y Moderna) se pueden administrar de manera segura incluso a personas con alergias a alimentos o medicamentos (...) 

El equipo señaló que las reacciones alérgicas a las vacunas son raras (aproximadamente 1,3 por millón de personas). Las reacciones alérgicas a las dos vacunas COVID-19 tendrán una tasa igualmente baja, según el equipo de investigadores. Sin embargo, recomiendan que las personas con antecedentes de anafilaxia a un medicamento inyectable o una vacuna que contenga polietilenglicol o polisorbato hablen primero con un alergólogo antes de vacunarse (...) 

La FDA recomendó que las vacunas se retengan solo a las personas con antecedentes de reacciones alérgicas graves a cualquier componente de la vacuna COVID-19.”

📌 hms.harvard.edu “Los hallazgos se publicaron en línea en la revista Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice.”

[Internacionales] Las autoridades de Noruega pidieron a los médicos que realicen evaluaciones más exhaustivas de los pacientes ancianos frágiles que esperan recibir la vacuna contra el #Covid-19 de la farmacéutica estadounidense Pfizer y su socio alemán BioNTech, tras la muerte de 23 ancianos poco después de recibir el fármaco, según informó este viernes la revista científica The #BMJ.

«Puede ser una coincidencia, pero no estamos seguros», declaró el director médico de la Agencia Noruega de Medicamentos (#NOMA), Steinar Madsen. «No existe una conexión segura entre estas muertes y la vacuna», subrayó.

Al investigar hasta ahora 13 de las muertes, la NOMA concluyó que las reacciones adversas comunes a las vacunas que se basan en una nueva tecnología ARN mensajero (#ARNm), como la de #Pfizer, pueden haber contribuido a desenlaces fatales en algunos de los pacientes frágiles. Estas reacciones adversas incluyen fiebre, náuseas y diarrea, reseñó RT.

Gov. Andrew Cuomo Monday re: Vaccine allocation - “We will allocate more doses to the faster, better performing facilities. Those that can vaccinate faster will get more of the allocation,” Cuomo said. 

“Again, facilities with slower vaccination rates will get less of new allocation. Our allocation is nowhere near enough, you want to maximize it, so places that can get it out first will get priority.” 

The weekly vaccine allocation by the federal government to New York State (numbers rounded up):

Dec. 14-20: 170,000.
Dec. 21-27: 467,000.
Dec. 28- Jan. 3: 274,000.
Jan. 4 – 10: 240,000.
Jan. 11 – 17: 240,000. 

That allocation from the federal government is not high enough. There are 7.1 million New Yorkers eligible for vaccines. At the current rate of allocation, it will take 6 to 7 months for those people to get vaccinated. “The federal government must increase supply to the states now.” Cuomo crafted a letter today, which was sent to the chairman of Pfizer, asking if New York can buy directly from Pfizer.
